headline: Bangladesh pacers rock Australia with four wickets before lunch on Day 1
summary: Bangladesh's pace attack, led by Hasan Mahmud, Ebadot Hossain, and Taskin Ahmed, ripped through Australia's top order, leaving them at 74-4 at lunch on Day 1 of the first Test in Darwin.
details: Hasan Mahmud struck twice, while Ebadot Hossain and Taskin Ahmed picked up one wicket each, reducing Australia to 74-4 at lunch on Day 1 of the opening Test in Darwin. This strong performance came after Bangladesh lost the toss and were asked to field first.

Australia's openers, Jake Weatherald and Travis Head, initially looked to build a foundation. However, Hasan Mahmud broke the partnership, dismissing Weatherald for 23 in the 12th over, caught by wicketkeeper Litton Das.

Hasan continued his excellent spell, removing the aggressive Travis Head for 22 in the 14th over, bowling him around the wicket. This double strike reduced Australia to 52-2 and shifted momentum firmly to Bangladesh.

Despite a dropped catch by Tanzid Tamim at slip, denying Steven Smith on two, Bangladesh maintained pressure. Ebadot Hossain then claimed the crucial wicket of Marnus Labuschagne for just one, caught by Shanto at second slip.

The impressive session concluded with Taskin Ahmed dismissing Cameron Green for 13 at the stroke of lunch. Green's dismissal gave Bangladesh their fourth wicket, capping off a dominant performance by the Tigers' pacers.

This Test marks Bangladesh's first on Australian soil in 23 years. The team has opted for a pace-heavy attack with Taskin Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud, and Ebadot Hossain, supported by spinners Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Taijul Islam.

headline: Gas shortage deepens Bangladesh power crisis, load-shedding hits 3,592MW
summary: Bangladesh is grappling with an intensifying power crisis as gas shortages lead to widespread load-shedding. This has resulted in daily disruptions, affecting both vehicle fuel and household cooking.
details: Bangladesh is facing a severe power crisis due to a deepening gas shortage. Load-shedding has escalated, reaching a peak of 3,592MW, significantly impacting electricity supply nationwide.

This energy deficit is causing widespread disruptions in daily life across the country. Citizens are experiencing long queues at CNG stations for vehicle fuel, and many households report a complete lack of gas supply for cooking stoves.

The crisis highlights the vulnerabilities of Bangladesh's energy sector, which is heavily reliant on imported fuel. This single shortage has created widespread distress and challenges in both the gas and electricity supply systems.
